messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Matching the results of a STAN ODE model with a different ODE solver?
parts:
Hi,

I'm working on an ODE-based model, and wanted to validate it. The best practice is to create a data generator, and so I attempted to do so, but I can't replicate the dynamics of an ODE model.

As a basic example, I used DeSolve to try to replicate the basic dynamics of Michael Betancourt's model, posted in another thread; it is attached. I run the model, and then use the predicted values to populate the DESolve model, and it doesn't match.

Is there a reason that I see large differences in the models? Is it just numeric inaccuracy, and if so, how can I reduce the STAN model's numeric error? (Or is there a bug in my code?)

Thanks,
David

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Matching the results of a STAN ODE model with a different ODE solver?
parts:
I'm still not clear on what you're trying to do.

You sent us a Stan model that involves an ODE, whereas deSolve is
a diff eq solver (among other things). What are you trying
to match?

To just run Stan's diff eq solver, you can have an empty model and
parameters and just run the generated quantities (there's a special
flag for models with no parameters). That will let you just run the
solver without the associated derivatives and gradients and Bayesian
posterior fitting.

- Bob

I'm trying to match the time series of measurements by using the parameters; if the input parameters match, the output time series should match.

In this case, I can generate whatever STAN results I want, perhaps using an empty model as suggested, but when I input the same initial state and transition parameters into a different ODE solver, I should get the same time series as a result. messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Matching the results of a STAN ODE model with a different ODE solver?
parts:
I don't think there's anything at all tricky about it. You
just need to write the diff eqs as a Stan function and provide
the data and parameters as data. Then you'll get the same answers
to within tolerance as any other working ODE solver (at least for
non-stiff cases Stan can solve).

- Bob

P.S. It's "Stan", not "STAN", unless you're shouting.

> On Nov 30, 2015, at 4:04 PM, David Manheim <davidm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I'm trying to match the time series of measurements by using the parameters; if the input parameters match, the output time series should match.
>
> In this case, I can generate whatever STAN results I want, perhaps using an empty model as suggested, but when I input the same initial state and transition parameters into a different ODE solver, I should get the same time series as a result. I don't right now, which tells me that I'm specifying something wrong. Since I'm more comfortable with the (simpler) DeSolve setup, I'm guessing it's the STAN model that I'm mis-understanding, and therefore mis-specifying. I'd like to be able to match the results.
>
> Once I can do this, as a next step I'm planning on using the data generator specified in R to make sure my model converges when excluding certain features in the actual data that cause identifiability issues. (Silly simple example: If I have three quantities that are multiplied to generate the data, I should be able to .estimate their product, even if I can't estimate the individual values.
>
> Is that clearer? Am I confused somewhere about how I should go about this?
>
> On Monday, November 30, 2015 at 12:34:34 PM UTC-8, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> I'm still not clear on what you're trying to do.
>
> You sent us a Stan model that involves an ODE, whereas deSolve is
> a diff eq solver (among other things). What are you trying
> to match?
>
> To just run Stan's diff eq solver, you can have an empty model and
> parameters and just run the generated quantities (there's a special
> flag for models with no parameters). That will let you just run the
> solver without the associated derivatives and gradients and Bayesian
> posterior fitting.
>
> - Bob
